delta.comment: PR #325 review-fix (2026-08-10). SHIPMENT SAFETY: 117-F removed from the 124-S manifest. backlogit ShipShipment gates both destructive covering-feature operations - setArtifactStatus(feature, done) and the collectArchiveCandidateIDs sweep (feature + descendants + linked deliberations) - on EXPLICIT manifest membership (explicitScope, backlogit 133-F/133.004-T), so closing S1 would have marked 117-F done AND archived it while 14 of its 19 children remained queued in 125-S/126-S. All three Plan-1 shipments are now uniformly TASK-ONLY: 124-S = 5 tasks, 125-S = 6 tasks, 126-S = 8 tasks (19 total); 117-F is a member of NO manifest and REMAINS QUEUED until all 19 children and all three shipments complete. Hardening gained H10.4; review gained F13 (P0, RESOLVED) and F14 (P1, RESOLVED-with-mitigation). RESIDUAL F14 for Ship: returnUnreleasedFeatureItems is NOT gated by explicitScope and clears parent_id on a non-member ancestor feature's unreleased descendants, so closing 124-S will orphan 117.006-T..117.019-T from 117-F (recoverable relationship change only - no closure, no archival, no data loss); Ship MUST re-adopt them under 117-F via adopt_item after closing 124-S and again after 125-S, and verify parentage before claiming the next shipment. NEVER re-add 117-F to a manifest.

SUPERSEDES THE EARLIER "NEVER re-add 117-F to a manifest" INSTRUCTION IN THIS LOG (2026-08-10 cycle-3 redesign, H10.5). The prior event is preserved verbatim as history and must not be rewritten; this event is the CURRENT close contract for log-based consumers.

WHY IT CHANGED. The earlier instruction was correct for the topology it was written against: 117-F was then a covering feature with 19 children spread across three task-only manifests (124-S/125-S/126-S), so any manifest membership would have triggered the destructive covering-feature path while children were still queued. That topology was REPLACED, not patched. Task-only membership turned out to be insufficient anyway: returnUnreleasedFeatureItems is NOT gated by explicitScope and also runs for a NON-MEMBER ANCESTOR feature discovered by the featureScopeRoots upward parent_id walk, so closing 124-S would still have cleared parent_id on all 14 downstream tasks (reproduced on the real engine: ARM A orphans 14/14). The recorded Ship-side adopt_item repair was rejected as a P-010 role-boundary violation.

CURRENT TOPOLOGY AND CONTRACT. 117-F is now a CHILDLESS product umbrella. Its former children were re-parented to three ROOT per-shipment covering features - 118-F (127-S), 119-F (128-S), 120-F (129-S) - each FULLY COVERED by and an EXPLICIT MEMBER of its own manifest, with origin_feature=117-F provenance retained on every task and all 27 blocks edges preserved. 117-F is grouped to the three by related_to links (non-hierarchical) and is an INTENTIONAL EXPLICIT MEMBER of the FINAL shipment 129-S, where it is closed engine-natively.

That is safe precisely because 117-F is childless and root: featureScopeRoots cannot escape upward from it, and returnUnreleasedFeatureItems iterates an EMPTY remainder, so the cascade the old instruction guarded against is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE rather than merely avoided. Proven end to end against the real backlogit 1.8.0 engine: returned_ids=[] on all three closes, 64/64 and 196/196 assertions, zero non-archived residue.

DO: leave 117-F as a member of 129-S and close it with a single `backlogit shipment ship` as part of that shipment. DO NOT: re-add 117-F to 127-S or 128-S, give it children, or call adopt_item / re-parent / reactivate at any point - post-close backlog repair is neither required nor permitted (P-010). A non-empty returned_ids on any close is a REGRESSION: halt and escalate to Stage.

See docs/compound/097-S-shipment-task-only-safe-close.md ("Reconciliation - the FULLY-COVERED ROOT exception") for which contract applies to which manifest shape, and docs/spikes/2026-08-09-plan1-shipment-topology-proof/ for the executable evidence.

NOTE: this is a close-path contract correction only. It does NOT clear the six open P1s (F16-F21) that currently gate all three shipments - no shipment is safely claimable yet.

SUPERSEDES THE EVIDENCE AND GATE FIGURES IN THE PRECEDING EVENT (which remains the CURRENT CLOSE CONTRACT). The prior event is preserved verbatim and its close-path instruction is UNCHANGED and still authoritative: 117-F is a childless root umbrella, stays an explicit member of the FINAL shipment 129-S, is closed engine-natively there, and must NEVER be re-added to 127-S/128-S, given children, or re-parented via adopt_item (P-010). F22 (post-LOCKING failures terminate WITHOUT releasing the workspace lock: plan 3.2 routes BOOTSTRAPPING/RESOLVING/LAUNCHING failures straight to FAILED, bypassing DRAINING where lock release lives, while plan 3.4 never auto-breaks a stale lock and requires an explicit operator --force-unlock; the most likely first-run failure of all, no copilot exe on PATH, therefore locks the operator out of their own workspace) and F23 (119.006-T requires a 'cancel during launch' test that the single RUNNING -> CANCELLING edge cannot legalise) were raised by the tenth PR #325 Copilot review on HEAD 914cb214. A log-only consumer must NOT conclude that 128-S is clear after dispositioning F18 and F19 alone.

NOTE FOR LOG-ONLY CONSUMERS: F18 + F22 + F23 are ONE missing invariant (cleanup and cancellation are guaranteed only from RUNNING), and F19 + F21 are ONE contract-placement ruling, so eight findings reduce to two operator decisions plus F16/F17/F20. NO SHIPMENT IS SAFELY CLAIMABLE. Authoritative detail: docs/reviews/2026-08-09-copilot-cli-supervisor-control-plane-review.md and the PR #325 body.

It also falsifies the H6 property that the session journal is "gitignored local operational state": in generated workspaces nothing installs that rule. Gates 128-S.

CURRENT GATE MAP (supersedes any earlier map in this log): F17 -> 127-S; F18 + F19 + F22 + F23 + F24 -> 128-S (F22 may ALSO touch 127-S if the lock-release obligation lands on 118.005-T); F16 + F20 + F21 + F25 -> 129-S. NO SHIPMENT IS SAFELY CLAIMABLE.

TWO CORRECTIONS.

(1) THE PRECEDING EVENT'S "THREE RULINGS, NOT TEN" UNDERSTATED THE GATE. Clustering is real, but F16, F17 and F20 were never part of any cluster — they are independent decisions. A log-only consumer reading that line could conclude the gate was nearly clear after three rulings. It is not.

(2) NEW P1 F26, raised by the fourteenth PR #325 Copilot review of HEAD 045bbb7f, still outside the exhausted 3-cycle budget. The open set is now ELEVEN: F16-F26.

F26 (P1, OPEN): the close-path contract in docs/compound/097-S-shipment-task-only-safe-close.md instructs Ship to close these shipments with a single `backlogit shipment ship`. But .github/agents/_ship.agent.md prohibits that operation UNCONDITIONALLY ("NEVER the cascade backlogit_ship_shipment, P-015" / "Do NOT call backlogit shipment ship"), with no fully-covered-root carve-out; and P-015 in templates/policies/workflow-policies.md.tmpl states its prohibition and postcondition absolutely even though its Applies-when clause is scoped to partial-feature shipments. Under fail-closed P-010/P-015 the instructed close command is UNEXECUTABLE. A STAGE PLANNING ARTIFACT CANNOT GRANT SHIP AN EXEMPTION FROM SHIP'S OWN OPERATIVE PROHIBITION — the compound doc declared an exception without amending the policy, the Ship agent, or the shipment-reconcile skill, and then told Ship to prefer that document over its own rule.

SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE: the 64/64 simulation proves `shipment ship` returns returned_ids: [] under this topology — the safety of an operation Ship may never call. If closure runs through shipment-reconcile safe-close, the proposition that matters is different (archiving each manifest item in turn with an EMPTY protected set leaves the backlog consistent). The evidence is aimed at the wrong operation.

WHAT IS NOT AFFECTED: the manifest shape. Under safe-close the fully-covered-root manifest is still correct — the covering feature is itself a manifest item and there are no unshipped siblings, so the protected set is empty and safe-close archives exactly the release unit. F14's structural elimination stands. Contested items are the CLOSE COMMAND and the SCOPE OF THE EVIDENCE, not the topology.

F26 GATES ALL THREE SHIPMENTS, because closure is on every shipment's path.

THE FIFTEENTH PR #325 COPILOT REVIEW (HEAD 1f14795e) RAISED THREE NEW P1s. OPEN SET IS NOW FOURTEEN (F16-F29) OVER TEN RULINGS.

F27 - 118.005-T owns the single-active-session lockfile enforcing the H2/H4 invariant, but requires only a PID + process-start-time LIVENESS check and SEQUENTIAL contention tests. ATOMIC acquisition is never required, so the read-then-write TOCTOU window lets two simultaneously-started supervisors both observe no live holder and both write the lock - exactly the concurrent sessions the module forbids - while EVERY acceptance criterion passes. Remedy: an O_CREAT|O_EXCL exclusive create or an OS advisory lock, plus a SIMULTANEOUS-CONTENDER test. 118.005-T IS A 127-S MEMBER: this is the SECOND open P1 on the ELIGIBLE CURSOR, alongside F17.

F28 - 119.004-T's H7 anti-drift guard is LEXICAL (asserts no bind/listen token and no banned framework import) and is bypassed by socket.create_server, socketserver.TCPServer, asyncio.start_server and http.server.HTTPServer. This guard is the control that DISCHARGED F2, a CYCLE-1 P0 on network-listener drift, so that P0's mitigation is materially weaker than recorded. Remedy: a BEHAVIOURAL socket check, denylist demoted to a pre-filter. Gates 128-S.

F29 - 119.001-T makes subprocess.PIPE the DEFAULT child stdio, but the migrated contract is TTY-ATTACHED (start.sh:66 uses exec; start.ps1 inherits terminal handles). Piping makes stdio non-TTY, changing interactive prompts, input handling, colour and buffering, and T1/T2 never characterize terminal attachment - so the migration can pass EVERY assertion while breaking interactive Copilot sessions, falsifying the zero-observable-change premise of S1/S2. Remedy: inherited stdio or a PTY, a TTY characterization case, and a ruling on how ChildOutput journaling (119.005-T) degrades. Gates 128-S.
